SURFACE
Two-col ascii, tab-sep, decimal comma (European/German locale: "47183,554644" = 47183.554644). Col1 monotonic descending (max 47183.6 → min 1648.7). No header. Task frames col1 as Raman shift (cm⁻¹) axis for direct G/2D peak fit.

CONTENT
Tested decimal-comma hypothesis: 6-digit fraction after comma ("554644") rules out thousands-sep reading (thousands-sep needs 3-digit grouping) → comma-decimal confirmed, no risk there.

Tested "col1 = ready-to-fit Raman shift cm⁻¹" hypothesis against world knowledge: graphene G≈1580 cm⁻¹, 2D≈2700 cm⁻¹. Data max=47183.6 — 17x beyond needed range. Top-3 prominence peaks (mechanical finder): x=18858.0, x=10421.4, x=3745.1. None near 1580 or 2700.

Tested nm-wavelength hypothesis (532nm laser, shift=1e7·(1/532−1/λ)): plug x=18858/10421/3745 as λ(nm) → shift = 18267/17837/16127 cm⁻¹. Physically nonsense (no Raman feature there). Falsified.

Tested /10-scale hypothesis: 10421.395/10 = 1042.14 vs 2×Si(520.7)=1041.4 → 0.07% match. Strong hit for 2nd-order silicon substrate line (common under graphene-on-Si). So x=10421 likely = Si peak, not G/2D. True G/2D signal probably sits near tail of range (x≈1648-2700, matches sample rows 3546-3565) but wasn't prominent enough to hit top-3 global search.

Surface says "axis ready for direct G/2D fit." Content says axis spans way past G/2D region and top prominence peaks are dominated by other features (Si substrate, baseline). Mismatch confirmed.

CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH

MISREADINGS
1. Comma-as-CSV-delimiter misparse → doubles column count, corrupts both x and y. Evidence: 6-digit fraction after comma rules out thousands-sep; must be decimal. (falsified as real risk only if parser is comma-naive — flag anyway since file is Raman-software export, commonly German-locale csv tools do this wrong)
2. Assume col1 ascending (typical spectrum convention) → reversed peak order/index if code assumes sorted-ascending. Evidence: sampler stats explicit `monotonic_descending=True`.
3. Blind global peak search assuming whole 1648-47183 cm⁻¹ range is graphene G/2D window → grabs non-Raman-shift-relevant peaks. Evidence: top prominence peaks (18858, 10421, 3745) don't match G(1580)/2D(2700); /10 scaling of 10421 matches Si 2nd-order (1041.4, 0.07% diff) — survived test, points to substrate contamination not G/2D.
4. nm-wavelength misinterpretation of col1 → falsified numerically: computed shifts (16127-18267 cm⁻¹) not physical. Ruled out.
5. Fit should restrict window to ~1500-1700 cm⁻¹ (G) and ~2600-2800 cm⁻¹ (2D) rather than trust global peak-finder output — real G/2D region likely only in tail rows (x≈1648-2700, per input sample rows 3546-3565), never surfaced in given peak list.
